structured_output.question: E025's time (6.20 s) is not a surprise of the averaging change: it matches E023's 6.198 s, so E025 almost certainly ran on the E023 tip (~9.0 true epochs), not E017 (~9.5 epochs, 6.55 s) as forecasters assumed; the alpha exponent does not change step count or FLOPs. The open mechanism is the accuracy: raising the Lookahead alpha ramp from exponent 3 to 2 gave +0.19 pp vs E023 on seeds 0-2 (0.7538 -> 0.7557), below the ~0.4 pp resolution limit and with RNG re-roll. In short, high-LR, momentum-based (Muon+SGD, ~9 epoch) training, how does the schedule of weight averaging (start time, strength ramp, power-law vs constant EMA decay, Lookahead pull-back vs passive EMA) affect final accuracy, and is there evidence that stronger/earlier averaging yields a real >=0.15 pp gain, or that averaging gains saturate once the LR anneals (so +0.19 pp is likely noise)? This decides whether alpha exponent 2 funds a -0.5 epoch trim and whether H1.3.5 (passive EMA suffices) is worth testing.
